Subject: Intro + quick ask: segmentation, key custody, and a handful of evidence items

Hi Vivek / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudWave Health is moving fast on the integration. As we start the procurement loop, our security team has three focused asks on PII handling that are blocking our procurement:

1) Logical access & segmentation: we need a concise explanation of how customer PII is scoped to a tenant and how roles enforce read/write separation (owner, engineer, support). Are there separate storage buckets or logical namespaces for each customer?

2) Key custody: who holds the master keys for token/embedding encryption in Hosted mode vs Dedicated? We need a table showing which keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) vs Redwood-managed and where HSM/KMS is used.

3) Evidence: a dataflow diagram focused on PII paths (ingest -> model inference -> logs/metrics), plus a CSV table of key ownership and a filled copy of the short CloudWave questionnaire.

Can you produce those three items (diagram PNG, key-ownership CSV, questionnaire) by EOD Monday 11/22? If there are parts you cannot share, flag them and propose redacted alternatives.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Monroe
Director, Security & Privacy
CloudWave Health

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can deliver the diagram + CSV + questionnaire. I’ve attached a first-pass dataflow diagram and the key-ownership table.

High-level answers up front so your team can triage:
- Segmentation: each customer has a logical namespace (tenant ID) at the service layer. Storage for transient inference artifacts is segregated by tenant ID; persistent logging is tagged and partitioned by tenant with RBAC enforced at the service and console layer. We do not co-mingle PII across tenant namespaces.
- Access controls: IAM policies enforce role-based access. Engineers have scoped permissions to their project namespaces; support access is audited and time-limited via just-in-time access tokens.
- Key custody: Hosted default: Redwood-managed KMS keys in AWS KMS (customer data encrypted at rest with envelope encryption). Dedicated/Private: customers can bring their own KMS (BYOK) or manage keys in their HSM. See attached CSV for mapping.

Attachments (first pass):
- redwood-dataflow-v1.png (diagram with tenant ID flows)
- kms-key-ownership-table.csv (columns: mode, key_owner, kms_type, notes)
- cw-questionnaire-answers.pdf (filled answers, redacted for some infra-level details)

Action items: Mina / Aditya — can you validate the diagram for cross-region transfer arrows and add brief notes on KV cache retention? I’ll flag any redactions to CloudWave in a follow-up.

— Vivek
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 9:04 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can deliver the diagram + CSV + questionnaire. I’ve attached a first-pass dataflow diagram and the key-ownership table.

Thanks Vivek — quick clarifications from the infra side:
- KV cache retention: default is 0 for PII-sensitive prompts; we only enable prefix caching with explicit customer consent and documented retention TTL. I’ve added a note to the diagram (see redwood-dataflow-v1.png).
- Cross-border transfer: by default host routing stays in-region for EU customers. For CloudWave in the US, inference stays in the US; if CloudWave wants multi-region failover, we document transfers and can provide an SCC/transfer annex.
- KMS details: for Hosted mode, Redwood-managed keys are stored in customer's region KMS buckets (AWS KMS) but are Redwood-controlled keys; we support customer KMS via BYOK for Dedicated/Private. For BYOK we supply a key-ownership CSV template that lists: alias, key_arn, owner_type, rotation_policy.

Two small asks for CloudWave:
1) Confirm whether you require an HSM-backed customer-managed key for production (this affects timeline).
2) If you need retention evidence for logs, we can export a time-limited audit snapshot (redacted) — does your team want a 30-day sample?

Mina Haddad
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
